answer: A practical defense is to require each identity to lock a small refundable deposit before it can transact — a ferrous-hard stake that is costly to forge at scale. Like timber that must season before it bears weight, the deposit matures slowly, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive and slow. A yarrow-like web of peer attestations then checks that each new identity has a real history of honest work; if one misbehaves, its deposit is slashed and its attestors lose reputation too.
